recipes.name: French Silk Chocolate Pie
ingredients_raw: 2 (1 ounce) squares unsweetened baking chocolate, melted and cooled
1 prepared 8 inch pastry shell, baked and cooled

steps.text: Beat butter in a mixing bowl with an electric mixer; gradually beat in sugar until light colored and well blended. Stir in cooled chocolate and vanilla extract. Add eggs, one at a time, beating 5 minutes on medium speed after each addition. Spoon the chocolate filling into prepared baked pie shell.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: French Silk Chocolate Pie
raw_recipe.description: This French silk pie has a silky smooth chocolate mousse filling; top each slice with whipped cream and chocolate shavings for a decadent dessert.

video.description: In this video, you'll learn how to make French Silk Pie, a classic dessert perfect for any occasion. This video will show you how to make a creamy chocolate filling and bake a flaky pie crust. With this easy recipe, you'll have a delicious pie that will impress your friends and family.

review.reviewBody: The first recipe for French silk pie is incomplete, that is why there is not enough filling for a full pie. After you cream the ingredients listed you are supposed to whip the whites of the two eggs used into a merange type consistancy using 1/4 c sugar to help form stiff peaks. Then you are supposed to add the chocolate mixture to the egg white mixture which will give you plenty of filling for your pie with a taste that is heavenly and is so light and fluffy. The way French silk pie is supposed to be. This is a great recipe that is fast and easy to prepare and is a crowd pleaser every time.

The trick to getting a silky, not soupy and grainy filling is to beat it on HIGH speed for at least 3 minutes per egg WITH THE WISK ATTACHMENT, NOT THE PADDLE IF YOU USE A STAND MIXER!!! I used the paddle first for the butter etc. and then switched to the wisk. Beating for any length of time on a lower speed won't work. I used 4 Tablespoons of cocoa powder instead of going through the trouble of melting and cooling chocolate. Also only used 1/2 cup sugar. I also added 1/4 cup malt powder to the butter mixture before adding the eggs for a French silk malted pie. Superb!!!! Double the recipe and the alterations above for a standard premade oreo crust. Thanks for recipe.

I gave this a 5 star because the taste and consistency was perfect. I did have to do a few adjustments. The first pie I made I doubled the recipe and separated the eggs beating the whites until firm and then folded them in. The total time of beating for this pie was 50 minutes (I beat the heck out of it at each step). The finished product was a perfect consistency pie with a very grainy taste. So, I did it again only this time, instead of using the 3/4 cup of sugar, I used 1 1/2 cups of powdered sugar (actually I used 3 cups since I doubled the recipe the second time as well). The end result? A perfect, delicious, smooth pie.

I have a recipe very similar to this. The only differences in the ingredients are the amount of chocolate (3 ounces rather than 2 ounces) and vanilla (1.5 teaspons rather than just 1 teaspoon) and unsalted butter rather than regular butter. But my method is a lot more beating. I beat the sugar and butter for 5 minutes at high speed before adding the eggs. I add both eggs at the same time and beat for another 4 minutes. I then add the melted, cooled chocolate and vanilla and beat for another 8 minutes (6 minutes if using superfine sugar). I also serve with whipped cream and use a cookie crust (made with Nabisco Famous Wafers). I have made it this way several times and it has never come up gritty. And it is delicious!

This is a great recipe as long as you don't follow the directions. First of all, that thing about "thoroughly cooled" baker's chocolate? You'll wind up with a zillion lumps of undisolved chocolate if you do that. Keep it at least warm. After throwing out my first attempt, I opted for Hershey's unsweetened cocoa substitute. Second, and this is the biggest faux pas: DON'T toss the eggs in as instructed. Just put in the yokes and put the whites in a separate bowl with some of the sugar. Whip the whites and add the thoroughly blended rest of it TO the whites and blend. Finally, I substituted confectioner's sugar for the granulated for an even smoother texture. On-line conversion ran from 1 cup sugar to 1 1/3 to 1 3/4 cups powdered. I opted for 1 1/2 to make the math easier (3/4 recipe cups sugar = 1 1/8 cups powdered). I mixed the butter with 3/4 cups powdered and put 3/8 in with the egg whites. Top with whiped cream and viola! spectacular, creamy smooth French Silk Chocolate Pie.

I'm in love! I always make the chocolate pie for our (large) Thanksgiving family gathering, and I know this will be a huge hit this year! I appreciate the suggestions to increase the amounts of the ingredients for a more fully filled pie. I trebled the recipe to fill two 8 inch chocolate cookie crumb crusts. I use an organic granulated sugar, which is a little on the course side, and so at first I was concerned that the grainy texture would not smooth out, but by the addition of the two final eggs (obediently beating in for 5 minutes after each egg - thank goodness for my KitchenAid!) I could see that the texture was smoothing out. Indeed the result is a wonderfully silky, smooth and rich chocolate decadence! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!

So after reading a bunch of the reviews for this recipe, I was thoroughly confused as to which directions I should follow. To double the recipe for filling…or not? To whip the egg whites into stiff peaks…or just whip the entire egg in as is? After much consideration, the only changes I made were to the serving size (I changed it to 12, b/c I used a 9 in pan), the crust (I used an oreo cookie crust), and the method of preparation (I used a whisk attachment for the eggs and a paddle attachment for the other ingredients). I whipped each egg for 5 minutes before adding the next one. I ended up with a BEAUTIFUL, silky, heavenly French silk pie! I will DEFINITELY be making this in the future.

Outstanding. I used an oreo cookie crust. Followed another reviewers suggestion to separate eggs and whip up egg whites separately, then add them. So rich and decadent, very creamy.
A smaller pie crust may be better but it's not necessary to fill a whole pie plate because it's so rich.
My pie turned out perfectly thanks to Barb’s comment about separating the eggs and using 1/4 cup of the sugar to whip with egg whites before folding into chocolate mixture!

I make this every Thanksgiving and would be in a lot of trouble from my family if I didn't. I do half vanilla, half almond and the result is just plain awesome. 

You do need to DOUBLE this recipe for one pie, the first year I did not and had to use whipped topping for the top half of the pie. (Was still good) Be SURE to beat with the whisk attachment on your mixer for 5 minutes between eggs. I set a timer. This ensures a smooth filling with no grainy texture.

This makes an extremely rich pie and most people are fine with a tiny slice. But it is always the first one devoured!

I tripled the recipe and put it in 3 store bought chocolate cookie crusts. I followed another reviewers suggestion and whipped the egg whites separately. I also melted the butter and baking chocolate together in a glass bowl on low before mixing in the rest of the ingredients. After chilling I topped with whipped cream and chocolate shavings. Delicious, rich, and super easy to make.
Used large pasteurized eggs.
Luscious!!
it was amazing!
I had this recipe in a cookbook from 1950, lost the cookbook. So happy to be reunited with the best French silk recipe!

I searched through a lot of different French silk pie recipes before finally coming back to this one, and none of them say to separate the eggs and whip up the whites before folding in chocolate mixture. Like another user had recommend. It's just a matter of beating the butter and sugar until it's fluffy and making sure the chocolate and vanilla are cool before mixing. This is a delicious smooth pie and if I can make it, anyone can make it!
Easy to make and absolutely fantastic!! Highly recommend

So very disappointed. I was expecting a very chocolatey pie. Like a Marie Callander French Silk pie. This was too buttery and no where near chocolatey. I added about an ounce more chocolate than called for and still too light. The consistency was good, though.

Omg, this is delicious! I whipped it for 5 minutes after adding the first egg and then another 5 minutes after the second egg. Smooth, silky, chocolatey and scrumptious. I used a premade pretzel crust and the amount of filling was perfect. Thanks for such a wonderful recipe.
This recipe is a family favorite. I now want to make it for a family with several members who are Celiac. If I pour the filling into a pie pan with no crust, would it lift out okay, do you think?
